speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my assessment, have you noticed any trauma, insect bites, or new jewelry on that finger recently? Additionally, is the area red, warm to the touch, or do you have a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury. Can you tell me if you can still move your finger, and has the pain worsened or improved since the initial incident? Also, are there any visible deformities, such as a crooked finger or a bump?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Lag of the Distal Interphalangeal Joint). The history of forced flexion during contact sports combined with your inability to actively flex the DIP joint and the finger resting in extension is classic for this injury. I will order X-rays of the right hand to rule out an avulsion fracture before finalizing your treatment plan. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
